_note: Illustrative reference data for grounding. Qualitative on purpose: no exact GPA cutoffs or acceptance rates, which change yearly. Students must verify specifics with official sources.

majors.name: Computer Science
majors.about: The study of computation, algorithms, software systems, and how to solve problems with code. Mixes math/logic with building real software.

majors.name: Data Science
majors.about: Turning data into decisions using statistics, programming, and machine learning. Sits between CS, math, and a domain (business, science, etc.).

majors.name: Mechanical Engineering
majors.about: Designing and building physical machines and systems, from engines to robots. Heavy on physics and math applied to the real world.

majors.name: Business Administration
majors.about: How organizations are run: strategy, finance, marketing, operations, and people. Broad and flexible.

majors.name: Biology (Pre-Med track)
majors.about: The science of living systems, often a stepping stone toward medicine or research. Lab-heavy and detail-oriented.

majors.name: Economics
majors.about: How people, firms, and societies allocate scarce resources. Blends social science with math and data.

majors.name: Psychology
majors.about: The science of mind and behavior, spanning clinical, cognitive, and research paths.

careers.name: Software Engineer
careers.about: Design, build, and maintain software products and systems.
careers.outlook: Generally strong, though entry-level competition has risen; standout projects matter.

careers.name: Data Scientist / ML Engineer
careers.about: Use data and machine learning to find patterns and build predictive systems.
typical_background: CS, stats, data science, or math
careers.outlook: Strong, especially with solid statistics and engineering skills.

careers.name: Mechanical Engineer
careers.about: Design physical products and systems across industries (auto, aerospace, robotics, energy).
careers.outlook: Steady; robotics and clean energy are growth areas.

careers.name: Product Manager
careers.about: Decide what a product should do and coordinate engineering, design, and business to ship it.
typical_background: often after engineering, design, or business experience
careers.outlook: Competitive; usually reached after building experience elsewhere.

careers.name: Physician (Medicine)
careers.about: Diagnose and treat patients after extensive medical training.
careers.outlook: Stable demand; path is long and demanding.

careers.name: Financial Analyst
careers.about: Analyze investments, company performance, and markets to guide money decisions.
cons: long hours in some sectors (e.g., banking)

careers.name: Clinical Psychologist / UX Researcher
careers.about: Clinical: help people with mental health. UX research: study user behavior to improve products.
careers.outlook: Clinical: stable but credential-heavy. UX research: growing.

universities.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)
universities.general_guidance: Among the most selective in the world. Expects top-of-class academics, the hardest available course rigor, standout achievements/projects, and strong essays. Treat as a reach for almost everyone.

universities.name: Stanford University
universities.general_guidance: Extremely competitive. Looks for excellent academics plus distinctive impact and personal qualities. A reach for nearly all applicants.

universities.name: University of Waterloo
universities.general_guidance: Renowned for co-op and CS/engineering; those programs are very competitive and emphasize math contest results and grades. Other programs are more attainable.

universities.name: National University of Singapore (NUS)
universities.general_guidance: A leading Asian university; competitive admissions weigh academics heavily. Requirements differ by program and applicant region.

universities.name: University of Toronto
universities.general_guidance: Strong, large research university. Admission is program-specific and grades-focused; some programs (e.g., CS) are much more competitive than others.

universities.name: Arizona State University
universities.general_guidance: Large public university with broad access and many programs. Often a realistic match/safety option for solid students; honors college available for high achievers.
